clue.text: Routine for Jewish comedian, dull person sounding drunk?

indicators.note: a drunk slurs a word, so the S of the word for a dull person comes out as SH

parts.note: a stick, as in 'a dull old stick', is a boring person

explanation.surface: A question about a Jewish comic's act: is it just a boring man who sounds tipsy?
explanation.walkthrough: Slurring STICK the way a drunk would turns the opening S into SH.
explanation.definitionFit: Shtick is Yiddish-derived slang for a performer's familiar comic routine or gimmick.

clue.text: European run with Coe on the outside

indicators.note: the athlete's name sits outside the letter for run

parts.note: Seb Coe is the British Olympic middle-distance champion
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A European runs alongside Sebastian Coe, keeping to the outside lane.
explanation.definitionFit: A Serb comes from Serbia, a country in south-eastern Europe.

clue.text: Feature of vessel on lake is excellent, excellent!

indicators.note: in a down clue the first pieces sit on top of the letter for lake

parts.note: the tops means the best, excellent
A1 means first-rate; the 1 is read as the letter I
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: An enthusiast declares a boat on a lake simply superb.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-class) is written with the digit read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: A topsail is a sail set above the lowest sail on a mast, a feature of a sailing ship.

clue.text: Soldier in company wanting 'proper speech' spoken

parts.note: RP, Received Pronunciation, is the standard accent of educated British English
oral means spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: A soldier in his unit lacks a posh accent.
explanation.walkthrough: RP, Received Pronunciation, is the prestige British accent once thought 'proper'.
explanation.definitionFit: A corporal is a non-commissioned army rank, so a soldier.

clue.text: Puzzle given a couple of marks for wrong and right answers, we hear

indicators.note: the phrase is heard rather than read, so its sound gives the spelling entered

parts.words: a couple of marks for wrong and right answers
parts.note: A plus CROSS (the mark for a wrong answer) plus TICK (the mark for a right one)

explanation.surface: A teacher marking a quiz hands back crosses and ticks.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, A CROSS TICK sounds the same as the puzzle word.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrostic is a word puzzle in which the initial letters of lines spell out a hidden word.

clue.text: Teacher is funny, little child being first one to grin

indicators.note: the short form of child is placed at the front

parts.note: CH is a short form of child

indicators.note: funny means odd, so the letters are rearranged oddly

explanation.surface: A teacher is amusing and a small pupil is the first to smile.
explanation.definitionFit: In Alice in Wonderland this feline is famous for its broad grin that lingers after it vanishes.

clue.text: Old group allowing in church cat

indicators.note: the outer pieces let the church letters in among them

parts.note: a lot is a group or batch
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An old congregation lets a cat into church.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocelot is a wild spotted feline of the Americas.

clue.text: Work outside home with fine alloy sheet

indicators.note: the word for work sits outside the other two pieces

parts.note: toil is hard work
in means at home
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Someone works outside the house with a thin sheet of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin metal leaf, originally tin and now aluminium, is sold in rolls for wrapping food.

clue.text: Monster making one cautious — b*** hell!

parts.note: chary means wary, cautious
the asterisked word is shown only by its first letter
Dis is the classical underworld, or hell

explanation.surface: Someone frightened of a monster swears under their breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'b***' is a bleeped curse, standing for its letter B.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this sea-monster formed a whirlpool opposite Scylla.

clue.text: Trapped in ditch there's a bear

indicators.note: the word for 'a' is shut inside the word for the ditch

parts.note: a rut is a groove or furrow, a kind of ditch
per means 'a', as in 'five pounds a head'

explanation.surface: Someone spots a bear stuck in a trench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is not taken as written: it means PER, as in a price per head. RUPERT Bear is a British children's cartoon character.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert is the famous checked-trousered bear of British comic strips and annuals.

clue.text: Nice dean working for decades

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: A dean from the French city of Nice has been in post for decades.
explanation.definitionFit: Decennia is the Latin-derived plural for ten-year periods, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Molecular scientist may use this — only he cannot go wrong

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are set wrong, that is, rearranged

explanation.surface: A boast that only one particular molecular scientist is infallible.
explanation.definitionFit: Engineering at the scale of single molecules is the technology such a scientist works with.

clue.text: Fellow erred — wrong ingredient for home-made wine

indicators.note: the letters are put wrong, that is, rearranged

explanation.surface: A man made a mistake when making his own wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Blossoms of the elder tree are a classic country ingredient for cordials and home-brewed wines.

clue.text: They live in Europe and will be entertained by shouts

indicators.note: to entertain is to host, so the word 'and' is held inside the word for shouts

parts.note: hollers are loud shouts or yells

explanation.surface: People in Europe are being amused by loud cries.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollanders are natives of Holland, the Netherlands, a European country.

clue.text: Copper finally enters to pick up ruffian, one put down in a hot spot?

definitions.text: one put down in a hot spot?

parts.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it

indicators.note: the last letter goes into the word for ruffian

parts.note: a thug is a violent ruffian

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of copper

explanation.surface: A policeman finally arrives to arrest a thug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' and 'pick up' suggest police arresting someone; one means a last letter, the other means hear.
explanation.definitionFit: A rug is laid on the floor before the fireplace, a hot spot in the room.

clue.text: Mass of fish traversing lake

indicators.note: the fish goes across the lake, so its letters straddle the L

parts.note: the cod is a common food fish
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A shoal of fish crosses a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A clod is a lump of earth or clay, a solid mass.

clue.text: Part supporting heartless undertaking

indicators.note: heartless drops the middle letter of the word for supporting

parts.note: to be for something is to support it
an action is something undertaken

explanation.surface: Someone backs a cruel enterprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraction is a portion or part of a whole.

clue.text: Useful cockney chap

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the H at the start of a word

parts.note: something handy is useful

explanation.surface: A handy fellow from London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class London accent, known for dropping initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: Andy is a common man's name, and a chap is any man.

clue.text: Study English penned by theologian — it's awful

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, so the theologian's letters surround the rest

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theology degree
to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: A divinity scholar writes up an English study, and the result is terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dreaded is feared, so a terrible or frightful thing.

clue.text: Car being introduced earlier, not very unsafe?

indicators.note: the car is introduced into the shortened word for earlier
not tells us to leave out the abbreviation for very

parts.note: previous means earlier, coming before

explanation.surface: A worry about whether a car that came out early is somewhat dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not very' looks like a qualifier on 'unsafe'; it removes V from PREVIOUS, leaving PREIOUS, into which 'being introduced' puts CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something precarious is insecure and likely to fall, hence unsafe.

clue.text: Huge virile-sounding Turk

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, huge

indicators.note: only the sound of the word for virile is used, not its spelling

parts.note: manly means virile

explanation.surface: A description of a big, macho-seeming Turkish man.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmanli is the Turkish name for an Ottoman, a member of the Ottoman Turkish people.

clue.text: Journey's end sealed by sound of horn on a car

indicators.note: in a down clue the horn noise sits on top of the A
the last letter is sealed inside the horn noise

parts.note: toot is the noise a horn makes

indicators.note: the end of the word journey is its last letter

explanation.surface: At the end of a trip a driver hoots the horn of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Toyota is a Japanese motor manufacturer, so a make of car.

clue.text: Sinner finally welcomed to hot fires? Maybe Paradise!

indicators.note: to fire is to stir up, so these letters are agitated into a new order
finally points to the last letter of the word sinner

explanation.surface: A sinner at last enters hellfire; perhaps that is heaven to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fires' rearranges R (from 'Sinner finally') with WELCOMED TO HOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The afterlife promised to the faithful, heaven, is one example of the life hereafter.

clue.text: Sounding like a bird, not half quaint

indicators.note: only half of the word for birdsong is kept, the first half

parts.note: tweeting is the chirping sound of a small bird

explanation.surface: Something chirpy but only half as twittery, and rather sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' throws away the second half of TWEETING.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee is British slang for excessively cute, dainty or quaint.

clue.text: Terrible row about a fool losing head in station

indicators.note: the jumbled row goes round the other pieces
a terrible thing is a mess, so the word row is jumbled
the fool's word drops its first letter

parts.note: an idiot is a fool

explanation.surface: A dreadful quarrel broke out over a beheaded fool in a station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' rearranges the row as RWO, which goes 'about' the rest. RADIO TWO is a BBC national radio station, so 'station' is the definition, not a railway stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio Two is a broadcasting station run by the BBC.

clue.text: Fan wants victory immediately

parts.note: a win is a victory
now means at once, immediately

explanation.surface: A supporter wants their team to win straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' looks like a supporter; it is the verb meaning to blow chaff away.
explanation.definitionFit: To winnow grain is to fan it so the breeze separates out the chaff.

clue.text: Travel to sacred ground that is located by church

parts.note: to go is to travel

indicators.note: something ground is crushed up, so the letters of sacred are broken and remade

explanation.surface: A trip to a holy plot of land beside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like the noun for land; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: God's acre is an old name for a churchyard, the burial ground beside a church.

clue.text: Guy may be so enthusiastic

definitions.meaning: a guy is the effigy of Guy Fawkes burnt on a bonfire every November 5th in Britain

explanation.surface: A man named Guy might be keen.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy Fawkes Night in Britain sees a stuffed figure, the guy, burnt on bonfires.
explanation.definitionFit: Burning describes the bonfire effigy, and figuratively means eager and excited.
